title: Northbound 1:1 — API & Console strategy
content:
Context / why this 1:1 matters:
- Weekly deep sync with Marcus (eng lead) to align on three linked fronts: short-term latency regression, Console rollout priorities, Dedicated capacity autoscale policy adjustments — plus check readiness for a Private deployment POC.
- Stakes: product teams are seeing customer churn risk if small-request latency bounces up; Dedicated customers expect predictable tail latency; Private POC (regional bank) needs KMS + audit checklist by end of month.

Top-line goals for the meeting (2x asks):
1) Agree on root-cause investigative plan for small-payload p95 regression and immediate mitigations we can ship this week.
2) Decide Console rollout gating criteria for per-route tracing and rollout cadence for canary -> 50% -> 100%.

Prep (what I will bring):
- Latest p50/p95/p99 snapshots for text-gen API by request-size (0-32 tokens, 32-256, 256+). (Slack: #api-prod-alerts, thread TS-regen-03)
- Short list of possible mitigations ranked by effort: kernel selection rollback, temporary route-based throttling, prefix-KV caching enablement, force-quantize-path for model-variant B.
- Short doc summarizing Dedicated autoscale policy proposal v3 (attached) and capacity cost delta numbers.

Agenda (30 mins):
- 0–5m: quick status and top-priority unblockers
- 5–14m: latency regression — evidence, hypotheses, immediate mitigation playbook (who owns what)
- 14–22m: Console rollout gating — telemetry, opt-in vs force, trace sampling settings
- 22–28m: Dedicated autoscale thresholds (burst policies) + Private POc checklist items
- 28–30m: quick review of action items, owners, deadlines

Notes / data snippets to reference live:
- small-request p95 up from 120ms -> 210ms since 2026-02-18 deploy of serving-runtime v2.8.3 (model-variant B default).
- CPU usage on host pool gp4-small surged by ~35% for small batch sizes; GPU utilization unchanged -> suggests CPU-side scheduling/backpressure.
- We observed increase in context-switches on runtime worker threads (logs: /prod/runtime/threads/trace-20260220.log).

Hypotheses (quick):
- scheduling change in runtime v2.8.3 (thread affinity/timer resolution).
- new kernel selection fallback path causing extra CPU work for short sequences.
- KV cache warmup/eviction thrash for heavy small request distribution.

Immediate mitigations to discuss (ranked):
- 1) Rollback serving-runtime -> v2.8.2 in the smallest affected pool (low risk) — time: 1h, owner: Marcus/SRE (PROS: fastest revert; CONS: hides root cause).
- 2) Route-level short-request throttling (limit concurrent small requests) — time: 2d, owner: Aditi + Runtime product (PROS: buys time; CONS: customer-facing throttle).
- 3) Force-kernel B->A for short-sequence model variants via routing rule — time: 6h, owner: Kai (PROS: targeted; CONS: requires validated compatibility).
- 4) Enable aggressive prefix-KV caching for API route group alpha — time: 1d, owner: Marcus (PROS: cost down; CONS: possible cache correctness edge cases).

Console rollout decision points:
- MUST HAVE: token-level trace sampling + per-route latency heatmap available in console to approve canary.
- QUESTION: do we ship trace sampling default at 0.5% or 1%? (tradeoff: observability signal vs cost). My leaning: start at 0.5% for hosted tier, 1% for Dedicated trials.
- Auto-fallback UX: if canary sees >2x tail-latency increase, automatic rollback to previous console UI feature flag. Need to confirm rollback owner and how it triggers.

Dedicated autoscale quick proposals (for discussion):
- current: scale-up at 70% GPU utilization sustained 2m; downscale after 10m below 45%
- proposed v3: scale-up at 65% sustained 90s, downscale after 5m below 35% + burst floor to preserve warm workers (min 1 extra worker for 10m/day).
- question: what are acceptable cold-start tradeoffs for enterprise customers vs cost? (talk to sales for committed SLAs)

Private deployment POc checklist (bank customer):
- KMS integration: need HSM verification + key rotation docs (owner: security team, but we need to ensure our deploy scripts expose necessary hooks).
- Audit logs: per-token logging ON/OFF toggle + retention policy (customer wants 7 years lead).
- Network: VPC peering + egress controls + IP allowlist (ops task).
- Operator runbook: scheduled patch windows, emergency rollback playbook, contact list.

Open questions I want Marcus to commit to in the meeting:
- Which mitigations will we prioritize if rollback is refused by infra? (expect commit to either force-kernel or throttling)
- Can SRE carve out a 2-hour maintenance window tonight if we need to rollback? (I can coordinate with CS to warn customers)
- For Console: who will own the rollback automation? (eng-console or platform-runbooks?)

Action items (to capture live in meeting):
- A1: Marcus to decide by EOD today whether to rollback v2.8.3 in pool-alpha; if yes, SRE runbook ticket JIRA-4833. (owner: Marcus Bell, due: 2026-03-07)
- A2: Kai to prototype force-kernel routing rule and smoke test on staging (owner: Kai Chen, due: 2026-03-09)
- A3: Aditi to draft customer communication template for potential throttling/maintenance (owner: Aditi Rajan, due: 2026-03-08)
- A4: Console team to set trace sampling defaults and implement canary rollback hook (owner: Leah Martinez, collaborators: eng-console, due: 2026-03-14)
- A5: Product + Sales sync to agree on Dedicated cold-start SLA tradeoffs (owner: Aditi + Sam from Sales, due: 2026-03-11)
- A6: Private POC checklist sign-off: security to confirm KMS/HSM checklist (owner: Security Ops, linked: CONFLUENCE-PRIV-ONBOARD-21, due: 2026-03-18)

Notes-to-self / follow ups after the sync:
- capture any new telemetry requests as separate ticket and tag with JIRA-4832-observe.
- if rollback occurs, request postmortem template from SRE and schedule blameless review for next Wed.
- capture console rollout risk matrix and share with Marcus for sign-off.

Quick meeting close script (copy/paste):
"Thanks — quick recap: Marcus will decide on rollback by EOD; Kai will spike force-kernel; I'll prepare customer comms and own Dedicated tradeoffs sync. If we hit rollback, we'll push a short customer note and run the rollback playbook. Follow-ups in JIRA-4832."
